name: Morpheus8 Body

lead: Morpheus8 Body applies InMode's RF microneedling to the abdomen, arms, thighs and other areas, marketed for tighter, smoother skin, for instance after weight loss.

Insulated needles deliver radiofrequency energy to the dermis and deeper tissue, which providers say prompts collagen remodeling. A 2024 plastic-surgery review lists Morpheus8 and Morpheus8 Body among RF-based minimally invasive tools used alongside surgical body contouring, and a registered 48-person study examined RF microneedling for leg cellulite.

paras: It is a clinic treatment, typically done in a series of sessions, and sometimes used alongside body contouring. Results are said to develop over weeks to months as collagen remodels.
Temporary redness and swelling are common; burns, scarring and infection are described as rarer risks. Independent long-term data are limited.

angle.text: Morpheus8 Body delivers RF energy into the skin of the abdomen, arms and thighs to prompt collagen remodeling, aiming for tighter, smoother body skin after weight loss. A 48-person registered study looked at RF microneedling for leg cellulite.

lead: Morpheus8 Body is the body-treatment version of InMode's Morpheus8 fractional radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system, used on areas such as the abdomen, arms and thighs for skin laxity and texture.[1][2] People seek it to look firmer and smoother on the body: the aim is to tighten loose skin, soften the dimpled look of cellulite and improve skin texture, without cutting or sutures.

Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes the device as a handheld system in which insulated needles penetrate the skin and deliver bipolar RF energy, with the heat said to trigger fibroblast activity, new collagen formation and tissue remodelling.[1] The Body 3D tip carries 40 pins for larger areas.[1]

A 2024 plastic-surgery review lists Morpheus8 and Morpheus8 Body among RF-based minimally invasive tools used alongside surgical body contouring.[3] A registered 48-person study examined RF microneedling for leg cellulite.[4] Independent long-term data are limited, and many of the available studies are industry-sponsored according to Grokipedia.[1]
infobox: About 0.5 to 8 mm across the Morpheus8 family (per Grokipedia)[1]
Abdomen, arms, thighs; neck and decolletage also listed[1]

paras: Morpheus8 is a fractional RF microneedling system. Grokipedia lists four tip types, resurfacing 24-pin, Prime 12-pin, Morpheus8 24-pin and Body 3D 40-pin, and says the needles reach depths from 0.5 mm for superficial resurfacing up to 8 mm. It adds that body applications include the abdomen, thighs, arms, neck, decolletage and submental fat, and that cellulite-like dimpling on the thighs is a texture target.[1] That account is untrusted, AI-generated text, and its citations do not consistently match its reference list.[1]

Wikipedia describes microneedling in general as repeatedly puncturing the skin with tiny sterile needles, used for scarring and acne, with research ongoing and combined with minoxidil for hair loss in some studies. Radiofrequency microneedling is not described there.[2]

Grokipedia reports that InMode, an Israeli company founded in 2008, introduced Morpheus8 commercially around 2018, expanded body applications around 2020, was granted a US patent on the underlying fractional RF technology on 11 November 2020, received FDA clearance in 2020 for electrocoagulation and hemostasis, and in 2024 for soft tissue contraction, described as the first such clearance for fractional RF microneedling.[1]

Grokipedia says results build progressively, peaking around three months and continuing over three to six months, and that results are described as lasting one to two years, possibly up to three, with touch-ups suggested every six to twelve months.[1] It cites a retrospective review of multimodal RF treatments including Morpheus8 reporting tissue contraction of up to 25 percent at six months and 35 to 40 percent at one year, and journal publications reporting patient satisfaction above 80 percent.[1] These figures come from an unverified AI-generated summary and from largely industry-sponsored studies, and long-term data beyond 12 months are limited.[1]

A 2024 article in Clinics in Plastic Surgery describes an author's use of RF devices, including Morpheus8 and Morpheus8 Body, in body-contouring practice; it is a practice description rather than a controlled trial.[3] A 48-person registered study, started in June 2022, evaluated multi-depth RF microneedling for cellulite of the leg.[4] The Grokipedia source states that independent long-term data are limited.[1]

Grokipedia lists redness, mild swelling, pinpoint bleeding, bruising, tenderness and warmth as common effects that usually resolve within one to three days, and thermal burns, permanent scarring, infection, prolonged hyperpigmentation and fat atrophy as rare complications.[1] Contraindications listed there include pregnancy, breastfeeding, implanted electronic devices such as pacemakers, active infection and isotretinoin use within six months.[1] It also reports that the FDA has flagged burns, scarring and unintended fat loss as risks of RF microneedling devices.[1]

timeline.event: InMode is founded in Israel (per Grokipedia).[1]
Body applications expand and a US patent on fractional RF technology is granted; FDA clearance for electrocoagulation and hemostasis.[1]
FDA clearance for soft tissue contraction.[1]
